newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher after powering above 124.20.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher after powering above 124.20.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply higher on Tuesday after extending gains toward the close having broken above resistance at 124.20, traders said.
"The surge toward the close was partly due to technical factors. Some players who were surprised by the break above 124.20 rushed to build new long positions," a senior trader at a city bank said.
The rise in JGBs on Tuesday was triggered by buying of long-term cash bonds by corporate pension funds and public funds during the morning session, traders said.
The September ended at 124.30, up from Monday's close of 123.91. Turnover was 36,513 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.340 percent as of 0635 GMT, down from Monday's close of 2.380 percent.
Corporate pension funds were detected buying JGBs from all portions of the yield curve in the morning, a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.

The funds had been buying JGBs since about last week and there were rumours in the market that they were doing so in anticipation of a large inflow of funds from Monday, a trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
Some said public funds were also detected buying long-term bonds on Tuesday.
Public funds bought 10-year JGBs with about eight to nine years left until maturity in the morning, a trader for another foreign brokerage house said.
City banks were also detected selling short-term JGBs and buying JGBs in their place, the trader added.

Traders said the 193rd 10-year JGB was firm due to short-covering by dealers. There was some speculation that the 193rd JGB may become the new benchmark rather than the 190th, and this triggered buying, the second trader said.

Some traders said economists' forecasts for the Bank of Japan's June "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment, which reached the market late in the afternoon, was another positive factor for the JGB market.

Forecasts for the key manufacturers' diffusion index (DI) from economists at 16 think-tanks polled by Reuters averaged at about zero. Their forecasts ranged from minus four to plus four. The March tankan forecast that the manufacturers' DI in June would be minus one. The figures are due out on June 25.
Some traders said the negative forecasts given by some economists fuelled buying of JGBs late in the afternoon.

Traders said there were rumours that scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank had been scaling down dealing positions in short-term money market instruments and possibly Japanese government bonds and currencies to reduce exposure.
There have also been rumours that DKB may have been buying JGBs recently, the first trader said.

"DKB has been raising ample funds recently, but they have had difficulty increasing their loans, and there are rumours that they are channeling their funds (raised using short-term instruments) toward investment in JGBs," the trader said.
